skill.name: commit-helper
skill.description: Conventional commit assistant for Logseq Template Graph. It reviews staged git changes and suggests commit messages with correct type, scope, body, and footer.

content.value_statement: Writing clear commit messages takes time and rules are easy to miss. This skill reviews git changes and suggests Conventional Commit messages for Logseq Template Graph workflows.
actual_capabilities: Reviews staged git status and diff output to identify the main change.
Maps changed files to project-specific Conventional Commit scopes.
Suggests concise commit subjects with valid type and scope.
Adds commit bodies and footers when context, issues, or breaking changes require them.
Validates messages for tense, length, punctuation, and project conventions.
Provides templates for simple, detailed, and breaking-change commits.
limitations: It is tailored to the Logseq Template Graph project structure.
It depends on staged changes or supplied diff context.
It does not decide which files should be staged or committed.
It cannot verify issue numbers or project policy outside the local context.

use_cases.title: Prepare a focused feature commit
use_cases.description: Generate a valid commit message after adding classes, properties, templates, or documentation.

use_cases.title: Review commit quality before merge
use_cases.description: Check type, scope, subject length, and body details before submitting a pull request.

use_cases.title: Describe breaking template changes
use_cases.description: Create a commit with the breaking-change marker, footer, and migration notes.

prompt_templates.title: Suggest a Commit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one staged change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest a Conventional Commit message for my staged changes. Explain the selected type and scope.

prompt_templates.title: Validate My Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this commit message for project conventions: [paste message]. Suggest a corrected version if needed.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Detailed Commit
prompt_templates.scenario: Multiple related changes need a body.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the staged diff and write a commit message with a clear body and any useful issue references.

prompt_templates.title: Document a Breaking Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced change that needs migration context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Conventional Commit for this breaking change. Include the marker, footer, and concise migration guidance.

output_examples.input: Staged changes add a Recipe class and cooking properties.
output_examples.output: Suggested message: feat(classes): add Recipe class with cooking properties. Reasoning: new class functionality makes feat and classes the best scope.

output_examples.input: Staged changes update Windows installation documentation.
output_examples.output: Suggested message: docs: update installation instructions for Windows. Body notes can mention Scoop setup and corrected links.

output_examples.input: Staged changes remove a deprecated Customer class.
output_examples.output: Suggested message: feat(classes)!: remove deprecated Customer class. Add a BREAKING CHANGE footer with migration guidance.

best_practices: Stage related files before asking for a commit message.
Use the most specific project scope that matches the primary change.
Add a body when the reason is not obvious from the subject.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague subjects such as update files.
Do not mix unrelated changes into one generated message.
Do not omit breaking-change details when existing templates need migration.

faq.question: Does this skill write commits for any repository?
faq.answer: It can use general Conventional Commit rules, but its scopes are designed for Logseq Template Graph.

faq.question: Does it run git commands automatically?
faq.answer: It instructs the assistant to inspect staged changes with read-only git commands when the user requests commit help.

faq.question: Can it create commit bodies?
faq.answer: Yes. It adds bodies when the change needs context, issue references, or migration details.

faq.question: Can it validate a draft message?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks type, scope, imperative mood, subject length, punctuation, and breaking-change format.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What input works best?
faq.answer: Staged git changes work best. A pasted diff or clear change summary can also be used.
